title: D Major Scale
description: Add a second sharp. D major uses both F# and C#.

steps.title: Two sharps
steps.description: D major has two sharps: F# and C#. The notes are D, E, F#, G, A, B, C#. There's a neat pattern here. G major had one sharp (F#), and D major keeps it and adds C#. Each time you start a major scale five notes higher, you pick up one more sharp.

steps.title: Find D
steps.description: Press D4, the white key nestled between the two black keys just above middle C.
steps.hint: One white key to the right of middle C.

steps.title: The two sharps
steps.description: Press C#4 and F#4 together. These are the two black keys D major uses.
steps.hint: C# is the black key just right of middle C. F# is the first black key in the next group of three.

steps.title: Now the whole scale
steps.description: Play up from D: D, E, F#, G, A, B, C#. Two black keys this time, F# and C#. Any octave works.
steps.hint: Start on D and stay on the white keys, but swap F for F# and C for C#.

steps.title: The D major chord
steps.description: Play D, F# and A together. That F# in the middle is what keeps the chord major.
steps.hint: Thumb on D, middle finger on the black key F#, pinky on A.

steps.title: Count the sharps
steps.description: How many sharps are in D major?
